Two arrested for terrorism in Spain’s Basque Country

Reuters

18 October, 2026 01:00 pm IST

MADRID, Oct 18 (Reuters) – Two people were arrested on suspicion of terrorism offences in Spain’s northwestern Basque Country, police said on Sunday.

A 34-year-old man and a woman, 22, who are both Spanish but who have not been named, are under investigation after a police search on September 26.

“Among the items seized was information concerning security forces, as well as the potential location of a site containing materials — presumably weapons and explosives,” said a statement from the Ertzaintza, the Basque regional police.

Show Full Article

Police did not say if the suspects were held in custody. Both will appear before Spain’s National Court at a later date.

(Reporting by Graham Keeley;Editing by Elaine Hardcastle)

US wants Israel to ‘crack down’ on settler violence in West Bank, Rubio says

Reuters

18 October, 2026 05:30 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

WASHINGTON, Oct 17 (Reuters) – The United States wants Israel to do more to deter attacks committed by settlers in the West Bank, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday.

“We’re very disturbed by those images and what we’re seeing,” Rubio said. “We’ve asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff.”

His comments to reporters came after the widespread dissemination of video showing multiple individuals attacking Heidi Levine, an American photojournalist with the Washington Post. Levine was one of at least two people injured in the Friday incident, which took place as Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian civilians.

Show Full Article

European diplomats and a French mayor also were attacked in the occupied West Bank, Belgium’s foreign minister said.

The US State Department, Rubio said, has inquired about the event that included Levine’s attack. Rubio, who spoke to reporters before boarding a flight to Uzbekistan, said he expects to hear back from the US Embassy in Jerusalem by Sunday.

Israeli settlers in the West Bank have been involved in at least 170 attacks on Palestinians since September 27, around the start of the annual olive harvest, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli settlements monitoring group.

(Reporting by Gram Slattery and Jasper Ward in Washington; Editing by Sergio Non and Franklin Paul)

Hurricane Trudy gains strength near Mexico’s coast, but is expected to weaken by Sunday

Reuters

18 October, 2026 05:00 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

MEXICO CITY, Oct 17 (Reuters) – Hurricane Trudy gained some strength as it moved toward Mexico’s western coast on Saturday, with forecasters warning it could strengthen a little more overnight before beginning to weaken on Sunday.

The US National Hurricane Center said Trudy was about 115 miles (180 km) south-southwest of Manzanillo on Saturday afternoon, with maximum sustained winds of 100 mph (155 kph).

The hurricane was moving at about 10 mph (17 kph) and was forecast to approach the southwestern and west-central Mexican coast and pass near the coast overnight into Sunday.

Show Full Article

Hurricane conditions are expected in the warning area on Saturday night, while tropical storm conditions are expected to spread across the region on Saturday afternoon and evening, the NHC said. Hurricane conditions are also possible in areas under a hurricane watch.

Trudy is forecast to bring 4 to 8 inches (10 to 20 cm) of rain, with higher totals of around 12 inches, across parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco through the weekend, raising the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, especially in steep terrain, according to the NHC.

Outer rain bands could produce 2 to 4 inches of rain, with isolated totals of around 6 inches, in Guerrero and Nayarit, where localized flash flooding is possible, the center said.

The NHC also warned of dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves in areas exposed to onshore winds.

Swells generated by Trudy were already affecting parts of Mexico’s southwestern coast and are expected to spread northward toward the country’s west-central coast through the weekend, creating life-threatening surf and rip current conditions, the NHC said.

Mexico’s national water agency, CONAGUA, has officially classified Trudy as a Category 2 hurricane.

(Reporting by Stefanie Eschenbacher and Adriana Barrera. Editing by Mark Potter and Franklin Paul)
